fixes.what: The QA agent step carries no id, no step runs `jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq` over the action's execution file, and no step calls `.sdlc/bin/agent-transcript.mjs --recover qa-report.json` — so when the QA agent finishes without writing qa-report.json, nothing records whether the Write was refused, went to a path outside the upload list, or was never made. sdlc-plan.yml and sdlc-root-cause.yml both wire all three, and agent-transcript.mjs exists for precisely this case; QA is the one artifact-emitting stage with no transcript recovery, which is why run 36983695548 produced only 'the agent did not write qa-report.json' and dispatch-fix classified it error_type=unknown. Its SHAPES map also has no 'qa-report.json' entry, so --recover would need one (keys: verdict, issue, attempt, tests, acceptance_rollup, next_action).
fixes.fix: Give the QA agent step an id (e.g. `id: qa_agent`), add a step after it — `if: always()`, env EXEC from `steps.qa_agent.outputs.execution_file` — running `jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq "$EXEC" > qa-transcript.json || true`, add qa-transcript.json to the qa-evidence upload path list, and add a `--recover qa-report.json` invocation of agent-transcript.mjs in the judge job before the validate step; extend SHAPES in .sdlc/bin/agent-transcript.mjs with the qa-report.json key list. That makes a recovered report subject to the same validator and gates as a written one, and prints the tool-call metadata that lets triage tell a refused Write from a missing one.
fixes.diagnosis: The QA agent ran to completion and did its job; it just never wrote the one file the workflow gates on. The action returned subtype=success, is_error=false after 323 turns / 51 minutes / $20.19, so the step is green, and the agent left 24 evidence files in qa-evidence/ (a 636-line three-file Playwright suite, 19 screenshots, a HAR, a trace, plus an out-of-band better-sqlite3 check against the Electron registration). check-evidence.mjs then said the report could not be read and the judge's validate rejected it by name — but that is the last step of a long chain, not the break. The break is that nothing in the qa workflow looks at what the agent actually did. The action writes the full transcript to _temp/claude-execution-output.json and the log prints only a metadata line about it; sdlc-qa.yml gives the agent step no id, never runs jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq over that file, and never calls agent-transcript.mjs --recover. sdlc-plan.yml and sdlc-root-cause.yml both do all three, and agent-transcript.mjs was written for exactly this failure (growth-os #20: an agent that reported success and wrote neither expected file). QA is the one agent-emitting stage with no transcript recovery, so this failure mode is structurally invisible here: whether the Write was refused, was aimed at a path outside the upload list, or was simply never made is not answerable from anything this run kept. A prior instance is recorded in the workflow's own comment at sdlc-qa.yml:620-622 ('validate then said the agent did not write qa-report.json and triage answered with another browser session'), and the fix applied then tightened the artifact download — which was a different failure and is why this one recurred undiagnosed. I did not rule out a bad agent run, and I am not claiming one: the evidence shows the suite was built and run and the fix's guard verified working on both platforms, so the QA work is sound. What is missing is not the testing, it is the report and any way to see why it was not written. That is a defect in the pipeline's plumbing, so it escalates rather than re-running: a rerun would burn another ~$20 and ~50 minutes to reach the same dead end, and the next agent would have exactly as much visibility as this one did.
fixes.evidence: test job, 'Test it, adversarially': {"type":"result","subtype":"success","is_error":false,"duration_ms":3098783,"num_turns":323,"total_cost_usd":20.19} — success, then 'Did the evidence survive?' logs 'the QA report cannot be read (ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'qa-report.json')', and judge logs 'sdlc: the agent did not write qa-report.json'. Meanwhile upload-artifact reports 'there will be 24 files uploaded' and the qa-evidence artifact (ID 11218775655, 16569296 bytes) downloads intact in judge — so the evidence survived and only the report is missing. The workflow gap: .github/workflows/sdlc-qa.yml has no `id:` on the agent step (so no `steps.<id>.outputs.execution_file`, cf. sdlc-plan.yml:360 and sdlc-root-cause.yml:333), no `jq -s -f .sdlc/bin/transcript-summary.jq` step, and no `agent-transcript.mjs` call (grep for 'transcript' in sdlc-qa.yml returns nothing), while agent-transcript.mjs's own header names this exact failure ('ran 22 turns, reported success, and wrote neither work-order.json nor stop.json ... triage could not tell a Write that was refused from one never made'). Survived work, if a person wants it: PR #11 (OPEN, MERGEABLE, head b635e0f), artifact qa-evidence with qa-evidence/spec/{regexp,regexp-edge}.spec.ts + fixtures.ts, electron-variant-check.txt showing the guard returning 0 for `\`, `#\`, `#[`, `(` and 1 for `#mortgage` on better-sqlite3, and served-tree-probe.txt confirming the preview serves _pr/ at b635e0f with the guard present. Ruled out: transient/outage/limit (a 51-minute agent run completed with is_error=false, no 429/529/timeout, and prior_signatures is empty); a defect in the app's own code (served-tree-probe and electron-variant-check both show the PR's guard installed and semantically correct); a bad work order (work-order.json is intact on the ledger at version 1 and QA's suite maps to its six acceptance criteria).

fixes.what: The 'Finish — Test it, adversarially' rescue step (lines 551-582) recovers a session that ended without its result by re-entering the SAME session with `--continue` (line 574). When the session that failed is long or its context exhausted, that is the one session it cannot recover: in this run it attached to the failed session and returned in 59 ms with num_turns 0 and an empty modelUsage — it never called the model — then reported the identical error. There is no third path, so a QA run whose session ends without its result is unrecoverable by construction, and the failure packet cannot distinguish 'the model declined to call the tool twice' from 'the rescue never ran at all'. The evidence that would say which is written to the runner's temp dir and destroyed, because show_full_output is false.
fixes.fix: Stop re-entering a dead transcript. Drop `--continue` from the rescue step's claude_args so it gets a fresh context, and seed that context from what the run already preserved: the suite is uploaded to qa-evidence/spec/ by the 'Keep the suite with the evidence' step (line 617), so download the run's own qa-evidence artifact into qa-run/ before the rescue and tell it to re-run the suite from those specs and return the result. Additionally set show_full_output: true on the QA agent step, or copy /home/runner/work/_temp/claude-execution-output.json into qa-evidence/, so a future triage can read the transcript that explains why a session ended without a result instead of inferring it.
fixes.diagnosis: Nothing in QA's setup failed. The checkout, the dependency install, the app boot, the preview allowlist guard, the credentials step and the schema limits all succeeded; the failure is entirely in the agent's return. The QA session ran 408 turns over 91 minutes ($26.36) and the SDK ended it with subtype 'success' and is_error false but NO structured_output — it finished its turn without ever calling the StructuredOutput tool. The workflow's own rescue step, 'Finish — Test it, adversarially' (sdlc-qa.yml:551, --continue), then fired, attached to the SAME session (both steps logged session_id 5a9e2404-175d-445f-acd9-d9f97829c760) and returned in 59 ms with num_turns 0, total_cost_usd 0 and an empty modelUsage — it made no model call at all — and again returned no structured output. So 'no structured result to write', qa-report.json was never created, and 'Check that "Test it, adversarially" returned its result' failed the job. That is the exact failure mode .sdlc/bin/claude-args.mjs:304-306 already documents for a model behind the gateway translator ('Muse Spark ran 40 turns and ended "successfully" with nothing returned') — and here the mitigation built for it failed too. It is not a code defect, not a plan defect and not an outage: there is no 429, 529 or provider error anywhere in the log, and the gateway served 408 turns and $26 of traffic across 91 minutes without complaint. I am escalating rather than rerunning because nothing in the repository or the configuration changed, so another attempt repeats the identical 91-minute, $26 workload against the same model and the same 200k context window, and the pipeline's single recovery path has now been shown not to work; that is 'try again and see', which is not a rerun. I could NOT determine WHY the session ended without its result: the transcript is hidden (show_full_output is false) and was written to the runner's temp directory, which no longer exists. What survived is raw evidence only — an 18 KB Playwright suite (qa-evidence/spec/schedules-post.spec.ts, T-1 through T-13), 14 screenshots, two traces, a video and a 60 MB HAR. The deliverable itself — verdicts, acceptance rollup, bug list — exists nowhere. `resume` would be dishonest: sdlc-qa.yml only ever downloads that artifact inside the same run (lines 684/691, judge job), so a re-entered qa job rewrites the suite from the work order and pays the same 91 minutes again.

fixes.what: Line 239 guards setup-node's npm cache behind hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') != '' && 'npm' || '', to stop a zero-dependency repo failing on a missing lockfile. But hashFiles is not free and not bounded: it recursively walks the whole workspace, and by the time this job's post-job cleanup re-evaluates the expression, the QA agent has installed a full Playwright browser tree into qa-run/node_modules and the app under test into _pr/node_modules. The walk then fails with 'Fail to hash files under directory /home/runner/work/actual-budget-sdlc/actual-budget-sdlc', the post step is red, and - because a failed post step fails the job - needs.test.result becomes 'failure', which makes the judge skip validation, posting, issue filing and merge. Every QA run whose agent does its job therefore discards a finished report over a cache key for a package manager this repo does not use.
fixes.fix: Delete the cache: input at .github/workflows/sdlc-qa.yml:239 (and the now-pointless comment above it). The test job runs `node .sdlc/bin/ensure-deps.mjs` and installs Playwright under the qa-run/ prefix, so there is no root npm cache to key; dropping the line removes the failure and cannot reintroduce the missing-lockfile error the guard was added for. If a cache is genuinely wanted here, key it on a path that cannot grow - hashFiles('.sdlc/bin/package.json') - rather than a '**' glob over a directory an agent writes to. Same expression is copy-pasted at sdlc-plan.yml:176, sdlc-plan.yml:1083, sdlc-implement.yml:241, sdlc-root-cause.yml:197, sdlc-triage.yml:78 and ci-verify.yml:146; those jobs install less into the workspace root, but the guard is fragile for the same reason and should be swept in the same change. Add a regression test under tests/ that asserts the sdlc-qa workflow contains no '**' hashFiles glob, so the fix is proved by something that fails without it.
fixes.diagnosis: QA did its whole job and the run was still failed by a cleanup expression. The QA agent wrote a complete qa-report.json and 323 evidence files (112 cited, all present, uploaded as the 10.5 MB qa-evidence artifact), but it returned its result by writing the file rather than calling StructuredOutput, so the SDK reported error_max_structured_output_retries; the workflow's own 'Finish' session then returned subtype:success and still emitted no structured_output. Neither of those made the run red - both agent steps carry continue-on-error: true, and step 24 'Check that Test it, adversarially returned its result' concluded SUCCESS, which it can only do when qa-report.json exists and is non-empty. The one red step in the entire job is step 57, the POST-job cleanup of actions/setup-node, where the template at .github/workflows/sdlc-qa.yml:239 re-evaluates hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') across a workspace the QA agent had just filled with qa-run/node_modules (a full Playwright browser install) and _pr/node_modules, and the runner could not walk it. A failed post step fails the job; needs.test.result then read 'failure', so the judge job skipped Validate the report, Post the report and route, and File issues for out-of-scope bugs entirely and ran dispatch-fix instead. A good report that was never judged was thrown away over a cache key that guards a repo this project does not even use - it is a yarn workspace with no package-lock.json anywhere.
